alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism mimics DTG weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target <4.5) with low Free T4, plus tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes — a classic picture of inadequately treated hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting her levothyroxine. The 9 kg weight gain over the past year is being attributed to DTG, but untreated hypothyroidism is a well-recognised cause of weight gain, fatigue, and dyslipidemia. The elevated LDL (4.2), total cholesterol (6.4), and triglycerides (2.3) are also consistent with hypothyroidism. Switching from DTG without first correcting hypothyroidism risks unnecessary ART change while the true driver persists. Viral load is suppressed on current regimen.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise levothyroxine adherence and dose before attributing weight gain to DTG. Recheck TSH after 6–8 weeks of consistent dosing. Address dyslipidemia after thyroid correction before considering ART switch.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycaemia risk: BMI ≥25 warrants glucose monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycaemia risk factors before initiating or transitioning to DTG, including BMI ≥25 kg/m². This patient's BMI is 33, placing her at high risk. Guidelines recommend performing random blood sugar every 3 months for high-risk patients during the first 12 months. Her fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L, which is in the impaired fasting glucose range. While this is not yet diagnostic of diabetes, it confirms elevated metabolic risk compounded by obesity and dyslipidemia. No repeat glucose monitoring is planned.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor blood glucose at least every 3 months for the first 12 months given BMI ≥25. Reinforce lifestyle modification and reassess metabolic profile after thyroid function is corrected.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by >6 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF-containing regimens. The patient's last creatinine was 196 days ago (2025-08-12) and no renal function test has been ordered today. TDF is associated with chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. While the previous creatinine of 72 umol/L was normal, the >6-month gap without monitoring is a guideline deviation, especially in a patient with new-onset metabolic abnormalities and obesity.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR today to fulfil TDF monitoring requirements. Continue routine renal monitoring per guideline schedule.
